_comment: PLACEHOLDER copy for a Wise-only case study, added 2026-08-14. It is deliberately about itself: it explains what slot it is holding and how it is being shown, rather than describing work that has not been written yet. Placeholder prose that reads like a real study is a lie waiting for someone to quote it, and this site's whole argument is that its claims are checkable. No [NEEDS:] markers, because those mean 'a real fact is missing here' and would put this page in verify-gaps alongside the two studies that matter. Overwrite the whole file when the real study lands, or delete it with its entry in src/data/studies.ts and src/copy/studies.json.
title: A third study, reserved for Wise
standfirst: This is a placeholder. It holds the slot for a case study written for Wise, and while it is here it does one useful job: it proves a whole study can belong to one hostname.

contribution.detail: Placeholder. Nothing on this page describes work that has been done, and nothing here should be read as a claim.
Holding the slot for a case study written for Wise, and testing whether a whole study can belong to one hostname.

problem.heading: What this page is
problem.standfirst: Not a case study. A slot with the shape of one.
paras: Everything you can read here is placeholder text, and it will stay that way until there is a real study to put in its place. It carries no claims, no numbers and no screens, because a placeholder that reads like finished work is worse than an obviously empty page: it is the kind of thing someone quotes back to you.
The two studies on this site are the argument. This one is a fixture, and the only thing it demonstrates is the mechanism described below.

process.heading: How it is being shown
process.standfirst: One build, two hostnames, and a list that answers differently depending on which one you are reading.
paras: The site is prerendered once and a single deployment answers every hostname, so nothing about a page can be decided by the address it is served from at build time. What the address decides is which version of the page is visible: a small script sets the brand on the document before the first paint, and the stylesheet hides whatever belongs to the other brand.

Until now that mechanism had only ever carried a heading and a list of links. This page is the first thing that tests it with a whole entity, which means a tile on the index, a place in the rotation at the foot of the other studies, and a page of its own. On www.deesyn.com none of that appears and the site reads exactly as it did before.

The honest limit is worth stating on the page rather than in a commit message: this is isolation by routing, not by build. This page exists at its address on every hostname, whether or not that hostname offers a link to it. That is fine while every brand here is a different framing of the same work, and it would not be fine for work belonging to different clients, which needs separate builds rather than a better rule.

interface.heading: What replaces it
interface.standfirst: A study in the same shape as the other two.
paras: A problem worth solving, stated as an insight rather than a brief someone handed over. The explorations that were rejected and the reason each one lost. A complex flow made simple, shown as real screens. A specific personal contribution, and results with a number and a source attached. Then hindsight, which is the section most portfolios leave out and the cheapest one to be honest in.
That is the order the questions get asked in, and the layout enforces it: the sections are named slots, so a study cannot quietly ship without its heaviest ones.

impact.heading: Results
impact.standfirst: None to report, and nothing invented to fill the gap.
paras: There are no metrics here. Every number on this site is measured and carries the source it came from, and a placeholder is exactly where that discipline would be easiest to quietly drop.

The mechanism was built before there was anything to put through it, which is the right order here: the question was whether a brand-specific study works at all, and a fixture answers that faster than a finished piece of writing would. It becomes the wrong order the moment the fixture is allowed to stay.

The thing it proved is smaller than it looks. Showing a study on one hostname and not another is a matter of what gets offered, not of what exists, and this page is prerendered at its address on every host either way. That is a real limit rather than an implementation detail, and it decides what this approach can safely be used for.
